messages:
kim: Quick sync: prototype for the compact autoscale row is posted. Two open questions before we lock visuals: (1) should the min/max stepper be inline with the SLO slider or separated into its own column? (2) how explicit should the guardrail messaging be when a selection would breach a safety limit?

raul: Inline stepper looks dense on small screens. If we keep it inline, we should reduce label verbosity (use icons + microcopy). On tablet/desktop inline is fine. Suggest responsive behavior: stack on <720px.

anya: Love the responsive idea. Also the stepper increment feels odd for small pools (1 GPU steps are too coarse when min=0). Can we support fractional step indicator for small pools (e.g., show 0.5 as "burst credit" rather than actual GPUs)? Or maybe support a separate "tiny pool" mode that uses different controls.

dev-pr: Implementation constraints: hardware allocation is integer-only, so we can't actually commit fractional GPUs. If the goal is finer control for tiny workloads, we could show an estimated vCPU equivalent instead—purely informational. That avoids changing allocation logic.

mike: For guardrails, people get anxious when the UI blocks them. Instead of an abrupt modal, propose an inline warning pill: "This selection may exceed your safety cap. We recommend X but you can proceed." Provide a small "Why" link to the policy and a soft confirm (checkbox) if they really want to override. Keeps flow and reduces panic.

lexi: Accessibility point: the inline warning pill must be programmatically associated with the control (aria-describedby linking to the pill id). If we require a confirm checkbox for override, that checkbox must be focusable before the action button and include clear accessible text: "I understand the risk and want to override the safety cap". Also color+icon+text for the pill.

kim: UX suggestion for labels: rename the stepper label from "Min / Max" to "Capacity (min–max)" and keep the microcopy beneath: "Min: guaranteed; Max: can burst when available." Make sure the short tooltip explains "burst uses spare capacity and may incur additional cost".

raul: We should also show an inline estimated cost delta for max vs min on hover of the stepper: small text like "+$0.14/hr when near max". That was asked during trials.

anya: Note on the SLO slider: participants in tests interpreted the left-to-right position as "cheaperless reliable". Let's invert the labels so the left is "Aggressive (lower latency target, higher cost)" and right is "Conservative (higher latency target, lower cost)" — or at least provide clearer adjectives. Also show the numeric ms value prominently.

dev-pr: Technical: we can show live estimate for egress of cost but backend call rate needs throttling. Suggest client-side debounce 250ms before hit. Also warn about eventual consistency on cost numbers (they're estimates).

mike: Small mobile layout request: when stacked, keep the stepper above the SLO slider so the important allocation numbers are visible without scrolling.

lexi: For keyboard users, ensure stepper increments can be changed with arrow keys and long-press support. Also ensure the SLO slider has visible focus rings and a value tooltip that's read by screen readers when moved. Use role=slider, aria-valuemin/max/now, aria-valuetext including ms and estimated cost.

kim: Decision summary: responsive stack under 720px (stepper above slider), stepper labeled "Capacity (minmax)" with microcopy, keep integer allocation but show vCPU equivalents for tiny pools, inline soft-warning pill for guardrail breaches with aria-describedby link, override requires accessible checkbox, show small cost delta next to max on hover, SLO slider copy tightened and labels clarified, client debounce for cost calc.

ux-bot: Recorded outcome to 'autoscale-ux' card: "Compact row responsive stack + guardrail pill + accessible override". Assigned: @raul to update frames, @dev-pr to spec debounce, @lexi to a11y audit, @anya to run mobile tests.

kim: Thanks team. If anyone objects to the override flow please call it out now. Otherwise I'll mark this as the design direction and add acceptance criteria to the ticket.
